# NEXUS CLI v2.0. Full Documentation for LLMs and AI Agents

> Complete plain-text reference. NEXUS is an AI-native development framework
> by GDA Africa. The CLI is open source (Apache 2.0). It gives every project a
> structured brain and, since v1.0, serves that brain over MCP as
> schema-validated tools. NEXUS 1.x gave every project a brain; NEXUS 2.0
> gives that brain A Harness: the Nexus Harness, an execution harness that runs
> agents already grounded in your plan, rules and lessons, and shows you
> exactly what they knew and did.
> Canonical URLs: https://nexus.glenhalton.com (home), /harness, /docs, /mcp,
> /agents, /skills (browsable registry).
> Packages: @nexus-framework/cli v2.0.0 (Apache 2.0),
> @nexus-framework/harness v1.0.0 (proprietary license),
> @nexus-framework/skills v0.4.0 (npm).
> Latest release: v2.0 "Execution": the Nexus Harness, `nexus harness`, and
> `nexus agent "<task>"`. 850 tests, 24 commands, 19 MCP tools, 16 doctor
> checks. See "Versions & history" below.

## What NEXUS is

Scaffolding tools generate files; NEXUS generates understanding. `nexus init`
(new project) or `nexus adopt` (existing project) creates a `.nexus/` directory:

    .nexus/
    ├─ docs/            # 8 structured docs + the two hot files:
    │  ├─ index.md      # PROJECT BRAIN, status, backlog, vital signs, progress log
    │  └─ knowledge.md  # append-only memory, decisions, gotchas, patterns
    ├─ plans/           # durable multi-step work (+ _active.json pointer)
    ├─ skills/          # core/ custom/ community/, how THIS project does things
    ├─ state/           # session tokens, sensor cache (gitignored)
    │  └─ chameleon.json # v1.2, evidence from the UI generation handoff
    ├─ config.json      # v1.2, project UI generator preference
    └─ ai/              # master instructions every agent file embeds
    .mcp.json           # registers the nexus-brain MCP server

The numbered docs (01_vision … 08_deployment) carry YAML frontmatter with
`status: template | populated`; `nexus upgrade` refreshes template-state files
and preserves populated ones (the "smart file strategy"). Markdown is the only
source of truth, no database, no daemon.

## The MCP server (v1.0 headline)

`nexus mcp` starts a stdio MCP server ("nexus-brain"). Generated projects
register it in `.mcp.json`:

    { "mcpServers": { "nexus-brain": {
        "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@nexus-framework/cli", "mcp"] } } }

Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and OpenAI Codex read .mcp.json automatically;
Cursor users copy the entry to .cursor/mcp.json. The server is spawned per
client and exits when the client disconnects. stdout carries only protocol.

### Tools (19: 15 read, 4 write)

Read (15): nexus_wake, nexus_get_context, nexus_get_active_plan,
nexus_list_plans, nexus_get_plan, nexus_query_knowledge,
nexus_get_vital_signs, nexus_brief, nexus_doctor, nexus_list_skills,
nexus_get_skill, nexus_list_agents, nexus_get_agent, nexus_get_handoff,
nexus_project_graph.
Write (4): nexus_plan_tick, nexus_plan_note, nexus_add_knowledge_entry,
nexus_plan_verify.

nexus_wake (READ): Session handshake. Returns: deterministic token
  "NX-WAKE-XXXX-YYYY-MM-DD" (sha256 of index.md + knowledge.md +
  plans/_active.json + date), activePlan id, activePlanStatus, nextStep
  (first unchecked step), doctorErrors, doctorWarnings. Echo the token in
  your first response, `nexus doctor` (check D09) flags sessions without one.

nexus_get_active_plan (READ): Active plan: full markdown, steps array
  ({index, checked, text}, 1-based), nextStep. If none: a note suggesting
  nexus_list_plans or `nexus plan new`.

nexus_query_knowledge (READ): Args: query (keywords), category
  (architecture|bug-fix|pattern|package|performance|convention|gotcha|integration),
  limit (default 10). Returns matching entries newest-first: {category, title,
  date, body}. Use before architectural decisions and debugging.

nexus_get_vital_signs (READ): Live sensors: git (branch, dirty, last commit),
  files (stale folders), tests, packages. Fresher than the cached Vital Signs
  block in index.md.

nexus_brief (READ): Args: since (git date expr, default "7 days ago").
  Returns the markdown status digest (same as `nexus brief --md`).

nexus_doctor (READ): Args: minSeverity (info|warn|error). Returns findings
  [{id: D01–D16, severity, description, fixHint}] + summary counts.

nexus_list_plans (READ): Args: status filter
  (draft|approved|in_progress|blocked|done|abandoned). Returns plan summaries.

nexus_get_plan (READ): Args: id. Returns full plan markdown.

nexus_list_skills (READ): Installed skills across custom/core/community
  (deduped by precedence custom > core > community) with name, source, title,
  description, triggers, and (v1.3) category, invocation and gate. Match your
  task against triggers before significant work, or just call
  nexus_get_context, which does the matching for you.

nexus_get_skill (READ): Args: name. Returns the skill markdown from the
  highest-precedence directory containing it.

nexus_get_context (READ): v1.1 keystone. Args: task, agent?, maxChars?.
  Composes ONE scoped pack: the alignment gate (v1.3), active plan slice,
  top-5 knowledge entries ranked by task relevance (v1.5.1; previously
  recency), skills ranked by trigger relevance,
  vitals digest, and (when agent named) the docs from its context recipe.
  Deterministic, budget-capped. The `gate` section is composed before every
  budget-consuming section and is never dropped; when gate.required is true
  the gated skill is injected into `skills` with matchedTrigger "<gate>"
  regardless of whether its triggers match. RUN IT AND RECORD THE OUTCOME
  BEFORE WRITING CODE.

nexus_list_agents (READ): v1.1. Agent roles in .nexus/agents/ (precedence
  custom > core > community) with role, status, triggers.

nexus_get_agent (READ): v1.1. Args: name. One agent definition: context
  recipe, least-privilege tool allowlist, working agreement.

nexus_get_handoff (READ): v1.1. Args: agent (optional). Returns the agent
  pipeline (implementer -> test-writer -> reviewer -> doc-keeper, or the
  project's custom chain) and next: the agent the MAIN THREAD should dispatch
  after the current one finishes. Subagents cannot call subagents.

nexus_project_graph (READ): v1.6. Args: root (optional). Parses the project
  into the derived typed graph Requirement → Feature → Task → Evidence and
  returns JSON plus a markdown digest: which requirements are unimplemented,
  which tests prove a feature, what evidence backs a task. A spike.

nexus_plan_tick (WRITE): Args: id, step (1-based), checked (default true).
  Marks a checklist step; returns nextStep. Out-of-range steps return a clean
  error. Never hand-edit plan checklists when this tool is available.

nexus_plan_note (WRITE): Args: id, message. Appends a timestamped note to the
  plan's Notes section.

nexus_plan_verify (WRITE): v1.6, "Provable Done". Args: id, waiver
  (optional), timeoutMs (optional). Runs the checks declared in
  .nexus/verify.json and records machine evidence in the plan's Evidence
  section; a waiver records an explicit reason instead. Feeds D11 v2.

nexus_add_knowledge_entry (WRITE): Args: category (enum above), title, body
  (1–3 sentences), optional why, howToApply. Appends a formatted entry before
  the file footer; duplicate category+title is rejected (append-only discipline).

### Recommended agent workflow in a NEXUS project

1. nexus_wake → echo the token in your first response.
2. nexus_get_active_plan → work the next unchecked step; do NOT re-derive plans.
3. nexus_query_knowledge before decisions/debugging; nexus_list_skills →
   nexus_get_skill for task-matched how-to instructions.
4. During work: nexus_plan_tick / nexus_plan_note.
5. After non-obvious discoveries: nexus_add_knowledge_entry.
6. Without MCP: read .nexus/docs/index.md and .nexus/docs/knowledge.md before
   every task; update them after; never delete knowledge entries (append-only).

## The Nexus Harness (v2.0 headline)

NEXUS 2.0 turns the project brain into an execution platform. The Nexus
Harness (`@nexus-framework/harness` 1.0.0) is the execution engine. Its
license is proprietary ("SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE"); it is NOT open source.
It is built on DeepSeek Harness (open source, MIT): Nexus kept that engine,
the Cordis plugin kernel and the append-only session log, and added project
memory, visibility and polish. The upstream MIT base and its copyright notice
are preserved. Upstream v0.1.7 is merged with every Nexus addition kept.

Architecture: the NEXUS CLI (brain: .nexus/ markdown, the 19-tool MCP server,
the public ./mcp export) → `nexus harness` / `nexus agent` write a patch file
(.nexus/state/nexus-brain.patch.yml) → the harness loads two Nexus plugins,
`nexus-brain-context` (ambient context at step 1) and `tool-nexus-brain` (16
in-process tools) → agents run, every event lands in the append-only session
log → the web GUI shows the brain chip, grounding inspector, plan checklist
and subagent inspector. The CLI keeps zero dependency on the harness engine;
the harness imports the brain via the CLI's public ./mcp subpath (v1.4).

What the harness adds over upstream (finished):
1. Ambient brain context: at step 1 of every turn the agent is handed the
   active plan, next unchecked step, rules and conventions, matching lessons
   from knowledge, and a vitals snapshot, as <system-reminder> blocks. Zero
   tool calls spent getting oriented.
2. In-process brain tools: 16 nexus_* tools registered natively on the
   harness tool registry. No separate MCP process, no stdio hop; every call
   lands in the harness's own session log and token accounting. The agent
   can read and update the plan, tick steps, query past decisions, run
   doctor. (nexus_get_context, nexus_project_graph and nexus_plan_verify are
   not in the in-process set; context arrives ambiently.)
3. See what the agent knows: a header brain status chip (grounded? which
   plan?), a per-turn grounding inspector drawer (exactly which plan steps,
   rules and notes were injected), and a plan checklist in the side panel
   (steps turn green live, or tick manually).
4. Subagent inspector: a side-by-side live view of a delegated helper agent's
   transcript, tool calls and status next to the parent.
5. Local models in one click: an Ollama quick-add card in Settings → Models;
   local models run with no account or key.
6. Clearer errors and control: nested vendor error payloads unwrapped into
   plain, actionable messages; per-model on/off toggles; reasoning depth
   defaults to medium for predictable cost and speed.
7. Nexus Glass: frosted-glass panels, an ambient animated background, Nexus
   marks throughout; the default theme on first launch.
8. One install: packaged as @nexus-framework/harness 1.0.0 with automated
   build and release checks.
9. Stays current with upstream (merged v0.1.7).

Early stage (preview, not finished): grill mode (`dsh-grill-mode`), where the
harness interviews the developer on decisions, trade-offs and edge cases
before code. The foundation and tests exist. This is distinct from the CLI's
alignment gate and `grilling` skill (v1.3), which are shipped.

The three v2 launch commands (part of @nexus-framework/cli):
- nexus harness: opens the full web GUI. Auto-detects .nexus/, writes
  .nexus/state/nexus-brain.patch.yml, wires the brain into the harness, and
  serves at http://localhost:3080. Flags: --port <n> (default 3080),
  --no-open, --desktop (packaged desktop app). Prints a banner with project,
  active plan and mode. Falls back to `npx -y @nexus-framework/harness` when
  there is no local checkout. `nexus harness verify <profile>` (since 1.5)
  live-probes a local Ollama-compatible endpoint.
- nexus agent "<task>": one-shot, headless, unattended. Runs the harness
  `headless` profile with the brain patch: ambient brain context injected at
  step 1, the 16 in-process tools mounted; runs to completion, streams
  reasoning to stderr, prints the final result to stdout, exits. With no task
  it prints usage. `nexus agent list|new|install|remove|status|sync` still
  manage brain-grounded agents as in v1.1.
- nexus code: RESERVED for NEXUS v3, a planned interactive terminal REPL
  (streaming, approval prompts, slash commands). Today it only opens a
  preview of the terminal profile. Not shipped.

The harness is an additional way to run, not a replacement. Markdown is
still the source of truth, and Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity IDE and Cursor keep working
exactly as before via `nexus mcp`.

## Agents (v1.1 headline)

.nexus/agents/ holds brain-grounded role definitions (same ownership model
as skills: core regenerated / custom SACRED / community installable). The
core four: nexus-implementer (works the active plan), nexus-test-writer
(verification keystone, detects test setup via sensors, writes tests
matching 06_test_strategy.md, ASKS before scaffolding test infra, records
waivers), nexus-reviewer (cites recorded conventions; read-only), and
nexus-doc-keeper (brain hygiene). Generated as Claude Code subagents in
.claude/agents/; degraded to "Agent Roles" tables in instruction files.
Manage with `nexus agent list|new|install|remove|status|sync`.

Verification gate: doctor D11 "Unverified Done" flags done plans whose
Evidence section lacks test results or an explicit waiver; `nexus plan done`
warns on empty evidence. If you are an agent: match your task against agent
triggers (nexus_list_agents) and adopt the matching working agreement.

## Chameleon UI delegation (v1.2, opt-in)

`nexus init` is the interview; Chameleon (@chameleon-ui-lib/react, also by
GDA Africa) is the UI generator. NEXUS resolves the answers into an AppSpec,
hands it to Chameleon, and overlays the brain, tooling, CI, and tests around
the files Chameleon writes.

Opt in: `nexus use chameleon` (project), `nexus use chameleon --global`
(every project), `nexus use none` (opt out), `nexus use --explain` (what is
active and which config file it came from), `nexus init x --ui none`
(override one run). Resolution order: --ui flag → project .nexus/config.json
→ global ~/.config/nexus/config.json → none. A saved preference is STATED
during init, never re-asked.

Guarantees:
- Not a hard dependency. Chameleon is resolved from the environment at
  generation time (NEXUS_CHAMELEON_BIN → project node_modules/.bin → npx
  --no-install). Absent/older/broken → falls back to NEXUS with a printed
  reason. Every project still builds with --ui none.
- Capability-gated, not version-gated: NEXUS asks Chameleon what it supports
  and disables unavailable paths, so new Chameleon releases light up new
  paths without a NEXUS release.
- Validated twice before writing: locally, then `chameleon new
  --validate-only`.
- Recorded, not claimed: every --json envelope is written to
  .nexus/state/chameleon.json as generation evidence.
- Toolchain merged: NEXUS folds its scripts and devDependencies into
  Chameleon's package.json, which is what makes the generated lint script
  runnable.
- Native targets skip Chameleon deliberately: its tree is DOM-bound (Radix,
  MUI, react-router, Tailwind v4), so an Expo target opts out and says why,
  regardless of a saved preference.

Agent-block preservation (D12): CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are in NEXUS's
always-replace set, so init/upgrade/repair used to rewrite them wholesale and
silently delete the block `chameleon agents init` splices between its
<!-- chameleon:start --> markers. NEXUS now captures that block before
regenerating and restores it after; doctor check D12 flags a project where it
went missing.

## CLI commands (24)

Top level: adopt agent brain brief code consolidate context doctor graph
harness init log mcp note pack plan repair skill sync unpack update upgrade
use wake.

Project setup:
- nexus init [name]: interactive scaffold: strategy questions (project type,
  data strategy, framework, patterns, persona), full toolchain, brain, skills,
  .mcp.json, CI. Flags: --local, --adopt, --ui chameleon|none.
- nexus adopt [path]: add brain + AI config to an existing project; never
  touches source code. Flag: --force.
- nexus upgrade [path]: regenerate templates; preserves populated docs, plans,
  state (smart file strategy).
- nexus repair [path]: fix missing/corrupted .nexus files only.
- nexus use [chameleon|none]: show or set the UI generator NEXUS delegates
  to. --global writes it for every project, --explain names the config file
  it resolved from. Opt-in; the default is none.

Alive brain:
- nexus mcp [path]: start the brain MCP server (stdio).
- nexus wake [--quiet] [--no-active-plan]: handshake token; recorded in
  .nexus/state/session.json.
- nexus sync [--dry-run] [--json] [--scope]: run sensors, write the Vital
  Signs block (idempotent, fenced by NEXUS:VITAL_SIGNS comments).
- nexus plan new|list|show|start|tick|note|verify|done: durable plans;
  lifecycle draft → approved → in_progress → blocked|done|abandoned; `done`
  auto-appends to the index Progress Log. Templates:
  feature|bug|refactor|spike|chore. `plan verify <id>` (v1.6, Provable Done)
  runs the checks in .nexus/verify.json and records machine evidence;
  `--waiver <reason>` records an explicit waiver instead.
- nexus log (v1.6): append a Progress Log entry (--message, --status,
  --scope, --date).
- nexus note (v1.6): append a validated Knowledge entry (--category, --title,
  --body, --why, --how-to-apply, --scope).
- nexus graph (v1.6, spike): derived ProjectGraph Requirement → Feature →
  Task → Evidence as a digest, or --json; -f <file>.
- nexus agent list|new|install|remove|status|sync: v1.1 agent management.
- nexus agent "<task>" (v2.0): one-shot headless brain-grounded run.
- nexus harness [--port <n>] [--no-open] [--desktop] (v2.0): open the Nexus
  Harness web GUI with the brain wired in.
- nexus code (v2.0 reservation): placeholder for the NEXUS v3 terminal REPL;
  opens a preview only.
- nexus context "<task>" [--json]: prints the composed context pack
  nexus_get_context returns over MCP, without an MCP server running.
- nexus harness verify <profile> [--config]: checks whether a local AI setup
  described in .nexus/harnesses.yml is actually receiving what NEXUS sent it
  (live-probes a local Ollama-compatible endpoint).
- nexus doctor [--severity] [--fix] [--strict]: 16 drift checks D01–D16 (placeholders,
  stale phase, progress gap, knowledge bloat/staleness, stale/orphan plans,
  missing vital signs, missed handshake, skills drift, unverified done D11,
  clobbered Chameleon agent block D12, missing alignment record D13, context
  load over budget D14, manifest declaring something unused D15, docs and
  code drifted apart D16). CI exit codes.
- nexus brief [--md] [--since]: ~30-line digest: vital signs, drift, plans,
  shipped commits, suggested next actions.
- nexus consolidate [--check] [--archive]: generates knowledge-summary.md
  grouped by category; --check is a CI gate; deterministic, no LLM.
- nexus brain status|check: health dashboard; auto-invoke layer prompts when
  the brain needs sync/doctor.

Skills:
- nexus skill list | registry [--framework] | new [name] | install <source> |
  remove <name> | status. Since v1.5.2, `install` takes an npm package, a
  GitHub owner/repo, a Git URL, or a local path, with --skill <slug>,
  --framework <fw> and --force. Directories: custom/ (sacred, never touched),
  core/ (framework-matched, refreshed on upgrade), community/ (installed).
  Precedence: custom > core > community. Registry fetched live from npm.

Maintenance:
- nexus pack / nexus unpack: zip/restore .nexus/ backups.
- nexus update: self-update from npm.

## Brain-aware CI (deterministic)

Generated GitHub Actions workflows include:
- A PR job that runs `nexus sync` + `nexus brief --md` and upserts ONE sticky
  PR comment (marker <!-- nexus-brain-brief -->) so reviewers see brain state
  next to the diff. Non-blocking.
- A doctor gate: `nexus doctor --severity=error` fails the build on drift
  errors; warnings never block.
No LLM dependency anywhere in this tier.

## Skills registry (@nexus-framework/skills v0.4.0)

Skills are markdown files with YAML frontmatter (skill, version, framework,
category, invocation, triggers[], status, optional gate) and fixed sections:
When to Read This, Context, Steps, Patterns We Use, Anti-Patterns, then either
Example (reference skills) or Completion Criteria (procedure skills), plus
optional Validation and Notes. Coverage: 49 skills across 10 framework sets,
22 of them shared; next.js (8) and react-vite (12) complete; sveltekit/nuxt/
astro/remix/go/python/rust have starter sets. Programmatic API:
getSkillPath/getSkillContent/listSkills/listFrameworks. The registry is
directory-driven; publishing to npm ships skills to all projects immediately.
Full browsable list: https://nexus.glenhalton.com/skills
Skills also ground harness and headless `nexus agent` runs: the skills whose
triggers match the task ride in the ambient brain context.

SKILL_SPEC v2 (v1.3), two additions, both fully additive:

1. The invocation axis. `invocation: model | user` decides who may invoke a
   skill. It defaults to `model` when absent, so every pre-v2 skill remains
   valid and behaves exactly as before. `model` skills are reachable by the
   agent or the human and hold reusable discipline; `user` skills are
   reachable only by the human and orchestrate. The invariant: a user skill
   may invoke model skills, a model skill may invoke model skills, and
   NOTHING may invoke a user skill except the human. This keeps the call
   graph a DAG rooted at the human.
2. The `procedure` and `integration` categories. Until v2 every skill was
   reference, consulted
   before an artifact is produced. A procedure skill is a discipline the
   agent RUNS to completion: an interview, a diagnosis loop, a review pass.
   It takes `## Completion Criteria` in place of `## Example`, because its
   output is a changed state of understanding, not a file. A reference skill
   can be skimmed and partially applied with no harm; a procedure skill that
   is half-run has not been run.

Trigger matching is deterministic token-overlap scoring with ranked
admission. Write triggers 2-4 words, task-level, one per distinct case. A
long descriptive phrase ("creating a reusable React component") is valid but
will not match a real task string.

## The alignment gate (v1.3)

The most expensive failure in a project is well-built code that answered the
wrong question. The gate makes alignment a precondition for feature work.

A `model`-invoked skill may declare `gate: { plan_types: [...], record: "##
Grilling" }`. The `grilling` skill declares one over feature, refactor and
spike plans. A bug plan opts in at creation with `nexus plan new --major`,
which writes `major: true` to the plan frontmatter, plan type alone cannot
distinguish a data-loss regression from a typo fix, and only the human
creating the plan knows which it is. Chore plans are never gated.

The gate keys off STRUCTURAL FACTS, the plan's `type` field and whether its
`## Grilling` section is filled, and never off the wording of the task.
A prose classifier for "is this complex?" would repeat the D11 v1 defect:
a keyword sniff over agent-written text, gameable by exactly the agent it
targets. A gated plan is scaffolded with the record pre-seeded and marked
pending, so an untouched template never satisfies the gate.

Surfaces: `nexus plan new` warns and scaffolds; `nexus plan start` warns then
proceeds; `nexus wake` prints the gate in the handshake; `nexus_get_context`
returns a `gate` section (composed before every budget-consuming section,
bounded by construction, never dropped) and injects the gated skill into
`skills` with `matchedTrigger: "<gate>"` regardless of trigger match; doctor
check D13 flags a started plan with no record, `warn` by default and `error`
under `--strict`.

Nothing hard-blocks, deliberately. An MCP tool cannot compel an agent, and
refusing to start a plan would push the work outside the plan where nothing
can see it. Same posture as the wake handshake: visible, not impossible.

## Context load (D14, v1.3)

Every generated instruction file is context load: bytes in the agent's window
on every turn, spent whether or not they are relevant. D14 measures it PER
FILE, not per project, six harnesses load six different files (Cursor reads
.cursorrules, Claude reads CLAUDE.md), so a session pays for one, not the sum.
Warns above 10KB, errors above 16KB or under --strict, and reports
near-identical files as info.

Applied to NEXUS itself: the generated CLAUDE.md was 13.4KB, with the docs
table stated twice, "orient first" stated in three places, and a Workflow
section telling the agent to read four files by hand immediately after telling
it to prefer one nexus_get_context call. It is 7.9KB in v1.3, reference
material (knowledge entry format, category table, docs table) moved behind a
pointer into .nexus/ai/instructions.md, critical behaviour (the onboarding
protocol, the STOP gate on template docs, the workflow rules) still inline.
A generator test holds it under 8KB so NEXUS cannot trip its own check.

Also fixed in the same pass: the generated instructions documented the
knowledge entry format as `## [YYYY-MM-DD] category, title`, which
parseKnowledge cannot parse (it requires `### [category] Title` with a
`**YYYY-MM-DD**` date line). Entries written by hand to the documented format
were invisible to nexus_query_knowledge, to the knowledge section of
nexus_get_context, and to nexus consolidate.

## Versions & history

v0.1 (Feb 2026) Genesis: init/adopt, 6 frameworks (Next.js 15, React 19 + Vite,
SvelteKit 2, Nuxt 3, Astro 5, Remix 2), toolchain, CI templates.
v0.2 (Feb 2026) Intelligence: 8-doc system, project brain, knowledge base,
agent personas. v0.3 (Mar 2026) Skills: live registry, skill command.
v0.4 (May 2026) Alive Brain: sync, plan, doctor, brief, auto-invoke.
v1.0 (Jun 2026) MCP: nexus mcp server, wake + consolidate, brain-aware CI,
generated .mcp.json + CLAUDE.md. v1.1 (Jun 2026) Contextualized Agents:
.nexus/agents/ core four, nexus_get_context, D11 verification gate, upgrade
data-loss fix (preserve-by-default + automatic backups).
v1.1.3 (Aug 2026) patch: upgrade/repair normalize partial manifests before
generation, so older or backend-only (framework null) manifests no longer
render the literal string "undefined" into generated docs and AI config.
v1.2.0 (Aug 2026) Delegation: opt-in Chameleon UI delegation (`nexus use`,
`init --ui`), D12 agent-block preservation, 18 commands.
v1.3.0 (Aug 2026) Skills II / Alignment: SKILL_SPEC v2 (invocation axis,
`procedure` category, `gate` block), the `grilling` skill, the alignment gate
in `nexus_get_context` and `nexus wake`, doctor check D13, `doctor --strict`,
`plan new --major`, token-overlap trigger matching, the D14 context-load check,
a ~41% cut to generated instruction files, and the fix for the `nexus upgrade`
data-loss bug (isTemplate/isPopulated scanned the whole document, so any doc
containing a `---` rule plus the words "status: template" was overwritten).
v1.4.0 (Aug 2026) Open Surface: the brain tools behind `nexus mcp` are
importable directly from `@nexus-framework/cli`'s new `./mcp` subpath as
native TypeScript. Any embedding host can call a tool handler directly and
get a real object back instead of the MCP text-content envelope. Additive
only, no behavior changed.
v1.5.0 (Aug 2026) Self-Check: three new doctor checks, D14 (total context
load across docs/knowledge/skills/agent instructions, not one file), D15
(a manifest declaring something the project no longer uses), D16 (docs and
code that have drifted apart). Optional `.nexus/harnesses.yml` describes the
AI setup a project runs against so generated instruction files are sized to
fit instead of truncated after the fact. `nexus harness verify` is new: it
checks, for real, whether a local setup is receiving what NEXUS sent it.
`nexus context "<task>"` prints the same composed context pack the MCP
server returns, without needing a server running. `contract_version` on the
context pack is now documented. 807 tests, 20 commands, 16 doctor checks.

v1.5.1 (Aug 2026): knowledge entries in the context pack are ranked by task
relevance instead of recency.
v1.5.2 (Aug 2026): `nexus skill install <source>` installs from an npm
package, GitHub owner/repo, Git URL, or local path (--skill, --framework,
--force).
v1.6.0 (Sep 2026) Provable Done ("Capture, verify, and see the graph"):
`nexus log` and `nexus note` capture commands, `nexus plan verify` with
.nexus/verify.json machine evidence and D11 v2, the `nexus graph`
project-graph spike, a D01 fix. MCP surface grew to 19 tools (15 read, 4
write) with nexus_project_graph and nexus_plan_verify.
v2.0.0 (Oct 2026) Execution: the Nexus Harness (@nexus-framework/harness
1.0.0, proprietary, built on DeepSeek Harness), `nexus harness`,
`nexus agent "<task>"`, and the `nexus code` reservation for v3. 850 tests,
24 commands, 19 MCP tools, 16 doctor checks.

Note on 1.1.3 vs 1.2.0: the published 1.1.3 tarball already contained the
Chameleon work. It was cut while that work sat under an [Unreleased] heading,
so 1.1.3 shipped a feature set its own changelog did not describe. 1.2.0 is
the same code under the version it should have carried; upgrading from 1.1.3
to 1.2.0 changes only the version number.

## Requirements & license

Node.js >= 20. TypeScript strict, ESM only. CLI: Apache 2.0, open source.
Nexus Harness (@nexus-framework/harness): proprietary license; the upstream
DeepSeek Harness base stays MIT with its copyright notice preserved. By GDA
Africa (https://gdaafrica.org). Source: https://github.com/GDA-Africa/nexus-cli and
https://github.com/GDA-Africa/nexus-skills.
